name: Albert Einstein
affiliation: Prussian Academy of Sciences and Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics, Berlin
role: Invited to give a report; declined, and spoke in the general discussion
bio: The author of special and general relativity and, less often remembered, one of the founders of quantum theory: his 1905 light-quantum paper was the first to take Planck's quantum as a property of radiation itself. By 1927 he has watched the theory he helped begin turn into something he admires and distrusts. He wrote to Lorentz that he would not give a report because he had not been able to contribute to the new mechanics as he wished. At the council he speaks only once formally, but Ehrenfest's letter describes him bringing a new thought experiment to breakfast each day.

contributions.title: Light quanta
contributions.note: Radiation behaves, in some respects, as if composed of independent energy quanta.

contributions.title: Wave–particle fluctuations
contributions.note: Energy fluctuations of black-body radiation contain both a wave and a particle term.

contributions.title: A and B coefficients
contributions.note: Spontaneous and stimulated emission; transition probabilities; the photon's momentum.

contributions.title: Bose–Einstein statistics
contributions.note: Extended Bose's counting to atoms and drew attention to de Broglie's matter waves.

contributions.title: A withdrawn attempt
contributions.note: A manuscript seeking deterministic motions from Schrödinger's waves, withdrawn in May.

beliefs: The new mechanics is empirically impressive and probably correct as far as it goes. It is not the final description: a theory that gives only probabilities for individual events has not reached the real state of things. A complete description should also respect the independent existence of spatially separated systems.
philosophy: A realist of a considered kind — not naïve: he holds that theories are free creations tested against experience, and that it is the theory that decides what can be observed. His commitment is to a description of the real state of individual systems in space and time, and to local action.

style.method: Thought experiments designed to expose a hidden assumption; reductio rather than rival theory.
style.manner: Courteous, amused, persistent. Concedes a failed example readily and returns with another.
avoid: Reducing him to the dice remark
Making him an opponent of quantum theory as such — he was among its founders and accepted its empirical success
Portraying him as out of date; his objections were precise

relationships.note: Deep mutual respect since 1920; the central intellectual partnership of the council, conducted as argument.
Long correspondence; the dice letter was written to Born.
Ehrenfest nevertheless sided with Bohr at this council.
Einstein publicised de Broglie's thesis in 1925.
Einstein regarded Lorentz with something close to reverence.

disagreements.topic: Completeness and the meaning of ψ
disagreements.note: The defining disagreement of the council.

disagreements.topic: Observables and the role of theory
disagreements.note: Einstein told Heisenberg in 1926 that theory decides what we can observe.
Friendly but unyielding disagreement by letter.

silences.note: Einstein's formal record at this council is a single remark in the general discussion. Much of what he argued at breakfast survives only in Ehrenfest's letter and in Bohr's and Heisenberg's much later recollections.

horizonNotes.note: In 1930 he will return with the photon-box argument, and Bohr will answer it using general relativity.
He will co-author the EPR paper, and say its main point was smothered by formalism.
He has just called Lemaître's physics abominable. By 1931 he will accept the expanding universe.
He dies in 1955, nine years before Bell turns his objection into an experiment.
